coaching.headline: Two Orb Primes taken, both wasted — a 47-minute loss with the structure war lost 6 to 14. We owned the prime pit and never cashed it into the map.
coaching.team: The draft was close to even: jungle favored (Grux 51.5% into Yin), carry favored (Murdock 48.4% into Sparrow), with mid (TwinBlast 48.5% into Fey), offlane (Bayle 47.6% into Steel) and support (Zinx 50.4% into Riktor) a hair behind. We won the 16.5 Fangtooth fight (2-0) and kept the majors close (24-29 against), but still lost structures 6 to 14 — buffs that never became towers. Two leaks: Grux died 9 times and TwinBlast 6, handing the map back while we held the buff; and we're 4/5 physical with the film flagging Grux and Bayle for no magic resist into a 3-magical comp. We poked, they sieged.
coaching.whatShiftedIt: After Orb Prime the clock IS the buff — group five and break a tower lane immediately, don't go fish for picks into Riktor's chain-CC (pull, silence, suppress) while it ticks away. Either of those two primes converted into structures wins this. And someone past Zinx needs a magic-resist item — Fey's 81k went unanswered. Anti-heal was fine; we brought two and Riktor's the only sustain, so don't spend the post-game on it.

perPlayer.16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3: Murdock carry, 7/5/2 — the matchup into Sparrow read favored (48.4%), so this was Goldilocks324's to carry and it nearly happened. Two fixes: 5 deaths means getting caught out of position, and Goldilocks324 skipped Lightning Hawk, the missing meta core. As the main threat on a 4/5-physical team, Murdock needs the spike from the core, not extra raw AD off Necrosis/Spear.
perPlayer.a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Bayle offlane, 4/5/6 — no feeding here; the build is the miss. Xeebs ran Mutilator/Sky-Splitter/Tainted-Rounds/Salvation/Aegis and skipped the winning core (Overlord/Rapture/Cursed Scroll). Bayle into Steel is already a hair behind (47.6%) and off-core makes it worse — build to be the front that opens the fight on the tower, not a bruiser trading chip damage on the side.
perPlayer.10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Zinx support, 1/3/9 — Willy Guggenheim's best line of the night: 9 assists, 20297 mitigated, only 3 deaths. Nothing to fix in the play. Pick up Spectra to finish the core (Prophecy/Spectra/Orion). The loss was the team not converting the two primes into towers, not anything on Willy's end.
perPlayer.3f5ff0dc-b979-43cf-adb6-9c0a794c1b6f: Grux jungle, 9/9/5 — don't let the kills flatter it. The matchup read favored (51.5% into Yin), so 9 deaths was the play, not the draft. Grux stacked damage items (Manta Scythe, Terminus, Tainted Trident, Deathstalker, Vanquisher) and skipped both Basilisk and every point of magic resist into a 3-magical comp with Fey on 81k. Every one of those deaths handed back the prime control the rest of the team kept winning. Build Basilisk, buy one magic resist, and stop feeding the magic burst.
perPlayer.f18f388a-9781-46b1-a864-934b1128cf3c: TwinBlast mid, 2/6/7 — the lowest-impact line on our side. The Fey matchup read unfavored (48.5%), but 6 deaths with only 2 kills is getting rolled in a lane that was close on paper. The build made it worse by skipping Ashbringer and Imperator, two-thirds of TwinBlast's winning core. Surviving and hitting the power spike is the priority at 2/6 — build the core and stop dying for free.

threats: Chain-CC risk (3 hard-CC abilities, ~2.5s of lockdown): Riktor Riplash (pull), Riktor Shock Therapy (silence 0.8s), Riktor Skewer (suppress 1.25s). Don't group tight into it — stagger the engage and hold mobility/cleanse for the key one.
Heal-stacking: Riktor. Anti-heal is mandatory against this comp — we brought 2 items of it.
synergy: Our engage/CC: Grux Crush (knockup 0.5s), Bayle Kingslayer (knockback). Our kills come from landing burst INSIDE that CC window — whoever lands it, the rest must follow up immediately.
We have sustain (Zinx) — favor the longer fight where our heals out-grind them.
Our damage is 4/5 physical — predictable; the enemy itemizes one armor item against most of it. A magical pick would split their defenses.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.
